newsitem.title: UK: Ecuador debt moves higher, Bradys await U.S. data.
newsitem.headline: Ecuador debt moves higher, Bradys await U.S. data.

text.p: Emerging market debt remained positive on Friday, with Ecuador bond prices continuing their upward climb in London.

Brady bonds surged on Thursday after Ecuador's long-term foreign currency debt was rated B1 by Moody's Investors Service, higher than expected. This led to expectations that Argentina and Brazil, also rated B1, could be upgraded.
"Prices in Ecuador have moved a bit higher still," a debt trader at a U.S. bank said.
"Other than that we saw some light profit-taking ahead of U.S. durable goods figures," he said.
Dealers said Ecuador's discount bonds were up 1/8 point. They closed at 78 in New York trade on Thursday, in turn 3-1/2 points up. PDI bonds moved 3/8 points higher from a 71 New York close.

U.S. Treasuries lost ground in London, with the 30-year long bond trading at 102-10 compared with 102-14 in New York and Tokyo, although analysts expected it to move higher in the next few trading sessions.

Durable goods data for June are scheduled for release at 1230 GMT. A Reuters poll forecast a rise of 1.4 percent, versus a fall of 0.7 percent previously. But analysts said the data were known to be volatile and were unlikely to move the market decisively.
Bankers said investors appeared to have shrugged off the currency devaluation concerns that hit emerging markets last week.
After devaluations in the Czech Republic, Thailand and the Philippines, markets feared Brazil and Poland could be next in line. Prices on emerging debt and equity collapsed as a result.
But this week prices have regained some of the losses, partly due to a U.S. Treasury market rally triggered by comments by Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greeenspan.
"The currency fears have taken a back seat at the moment, but it does not mean they can't come to the fore again," a Brady market strategist said.

"For the time being the market is not focusing on it. The combination of Greenspan's testimony, the strong U.S. Treasury market and now Ecuador getting a better-than-anticipated rating has created client demand for Brady bonds once more," he said. -- Aline van Duyn, London Newsroom +44 171 542 7748
